interest: Reveals internal U.S. debates on diluting Zaibatsu deconcentration and controversy over privatizing the Japanese tobacco monopoly.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file documents U.S. State Department, Army, and SCAP policies concerning Japanese economic deconcentration, antitrust enforcement, and business democratization between 1947 and 1949. Key matters include internal debates over the dilution of deconcentration under Law No. 207 and the Dodge economic stabilization program, assessments by SCAP Antitrust Chief Edward C. Welsh, public and political controversy over Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida's plan to privatize the state tobacco monopoly with American participation, and SCAP directives releasing dozens of reorganized Japanese companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
